sources.title: Alfred W. Crosby, “An Enthusiastic Second,” Journal of American History 76, no. 4 (March 1990): 1107–1110.
sources.citation: Alfred W. Crosby, “An Enthusiastic Second,” Journal of American History 76:4 (1990): 1107–1110. doi:10.2307/2936587.

verification.note: Fresh selected primary reading: the publisher’s complete first-page facsimile, printed 1107, visually checked after OCR. Exact accessible publisher record https://oup.silverchair-cdn.com/article-minimal/896821 supplies author, title, journal, date, DOI and first-page preview. Its image is a signed CDN URL, so the stable DOI and record are retained. The body opens with agreement with Donald Worster’s Transformations of the Earth, proposes agroecosystems as an important historical subject, and discusses agriculture’s changes to biota, soil and water. Only p. 1107 was read. Pages 1108–1110, other round-table responses and Worster’s reply were not freshly read. Rhetorical references to Turner and Spengler on this page do not establish additional intellectual-debt edges.

sources.scope_note: Specified endorsement of Worster’s agroecological research agenda; first-page witness only.

source_addenda.pe131_cronon_uses_1993: Dedicated Crosby review, 2026-10-25: author-hosted scan freshly downloaded from https://williamcronon.net/writing/Cronon_Uses_of_Environmental_History_EHR_Fall_1993.pdf (the www URL returned 406). OCR-assisted selected reading of pp. 8–11 and relevant notes on 21–22; page images checked for p. 8 migration lesson, p. 10 introduced-pathogen lesson, and n. 16 on 21. Note 16 cites The Columbian Exchange and Ecological Imperialism; n. 25 on 22 cites both again. The inherited wording that collectively placed notes 16 and 25 on p. 22 is imprecise: their actual folios are 21 and 22. The old note is retained; this addition records the precise fresh check. This is a specified resource claim, not complete intellectual descent or a fresh full reading of either Crosby book.
source_addenda.pe131_worster_jah_1990: Dedicated Crosby review, 2026-10-25: selected English primary transcription read at https://www.scribd.com/document/1022124209/2-1-1-Transformations-of-the-Earth-Donald-Worster-1990, printed pp. 1087–1089, particularly 1088 and n. 4. Page labels and note text explicitly identify Crosby’s ecological imperialism and the 1986 book; the Kentucky bluegrass paragraph simultaneously rejects a simple environmental-determinist reading. English page images were not seen. This is a new selected transcription reading, not a claim that the original English article or the round table was freshly read in full. The earlier full Portuguese translation, partial reprint and original access-failure notes remain intact.
source_addenda.crosby_ecological: Dedicated Crosby review, 2026-10-25: Cambridge’s 18-page second-edition front matter freshly downloaded from https://assets.cambridge.org/97805215/46188/frontmatter/9780521546188_frontmatter.pdf. The 2004 preface pp. xv–xx and acknowledgments xxi–xxii read through OCR; xvii was visually checked. Pomeranz’s The Great Divergence (2000) is explicitly identified in xvii n. 1 as the clearest exposition of the new scenario; the overseas-resource/industrialization argument continues xviii–xx. This evidence is dated 2004 and does not extend the claim backward to 1986. The acknowledgments distinguish encouragement from actual manuscript reading (William McNeill, absent personal endpoint, read the first draft). The original 1986 edition and chapters 2–12 were not freshly read.
